changelog: A hotfix on top of 0.0.48. One bug, and it was a bad one on a phone. **The phone got its pan back.** The camera rewrite in 0.0.48 replaced the board's scroll container with a transform. On a desktop that was a straight upgrade. On a phone it quietly removed the only way to move the camera: a one-finger drag used to scroll the board natively, and afterwards there was nothing left to scroll. Two-finger pinch still zoomed, and nothing panned at all — on a large map most of the battlefield was simply unreachable. One finger now drags the board directly, with the ground following your finger. The care in that fix is in keeping a drag distinguishable from a **tap**, because tapping a tile is how the game is played. A touch only becomes a pan after it has travelled far enough that you clearly meant it, a second finger landing hands the gesture to the pinch, and the click a browser fires at the end of a drag is swallowed so a pan cannot finish by selecting whatever tile you stopped on. That last part needed one more turn of the screw. The trap that swallows the post-pan click was armed on a timer, on the assumption that a click would arrive to spring it — but WebKit, which is what both the Mac and iOS builds actually run on, fires no click at all after a finger has travelled. So the trap would usually sit there unsprung and eat your *next* tap instead: the pan works, and the order right after it silently does nothing. It is now disarmed the moment a new touch begins, so it can only ever catch the click of the drag that armed it. **Store copy** was held to the same standard as the game. The 0.0.48 pass renamed the swamp, the creature and the achievements; the store page still carried alternates naming three trademarks belonging to other publishers, and a note listing the very names that had just been removed. Both are gone. Nothing else changed. Everything in 0.0.48 — the performance work, the Graphics preset, the frame-time meter, the renames — is unchanged and still here.
